record: Payment step hangs after payment-api release 2.2.4. Ten minutes after the release the p95 latency rose from 240 ms to 1.9 s. Work notes: requests to the payment provider queue in the new HTTP client; its connection pool is 5 instead of 50 in 2.2.4. Resolution: rolled back to 2.2.3, latency normal after 25 minutes; fixed in 2.2.5.
explanation: Release 2.2.4 reduced the provider connection pool from 50 to 5, so requests queued.

record: Payments rejected with HTTP 503. Most payments failed; the provider answered with HTTP 503 and its status page showed a major outage. No deployment or configuration change on our side that day. Resolution: switched to the backup provider until the provider recovered.
explanation: An outage at the payment provider; nothing on our side had to be fixed.

record: Duplicate webhooks from the payment provider. Some bookings were confirmed twice and ledger entries were duplicated. Work notes: the provider re-sent webhooks after a timeout on their side; each copy was processed again. Resolution: made the webhook handler idempotent and removed the duplicate ledger entries.
explanation: Duplicate webhook events were processed twice and created duplicate bookings and ledger entries.

record: Refund amounts off by one cent. After payment-api release 2.1.0, about 3 % of refunds were one cent too low. Work notes: 2.1.0 changed the rounding of currency amounts from half-up to half-even. Resolution: hotfix 2.1.1 restored half-up rounding; finance corrected the refunds.
explanation: Release 2.1.0 changed the rounding mode for refunds.

record: All card payments rejected from 06:00. The provider answered every request with 401 unauthorized. Work notes: the API key of our provider account had an end date of this morning; nobody renewed it. The provider had no incident. Resolution: created a new key, stored it in the secret store, added an expiry alert.
explanation: The provider API key of our account expired and was not renewed.

record: Slow payments during the autumn sale. From 18:00 the traffic was four times the normal level; the p95 latency of payment-api rose to 3 s. All 200 worker threads were busy, the provider answered in normal time. No change that week. Resolution: scaled payment-api from 6 to 12 instances; latency normal after 10 minutes.
explanation: Four times the normal traffic exhausted the worker threads of payment-api.

record: 3-D Secure checks take 20 s. Card payments needed the bank's 3-D Secure step, which took up to 20 seconds for two large banks. Our services answered in normal time. Resolution: none on our side - the banks fixed their authentication service after 70 minutes; we informed customers on the status page.
explanation: The 3-D Secure service of two banks was slow; nothing on our side had to be fixed.

record: Payments routed to a test provider. For 25 minutes, 8 % of the payments failed. Work notes: someone switched the feature flag new-provider-routing on in production during a test; no release that day. Resolution: switched the flag off; flag changes now need a second person.
explanation: A feature flag was switched on in production by mistake and routed payments to a test provider.

record: Search results take 20 s during the morning peak. Many customers gave up. Work notes: at 08:00 the traffic was twice the usual level; all 40 database connections of booking-search were in use and requests waited. No change for two weeks. Resolution: increased the pool size and restarted the search pods.
explanation: A traffic peak used up all database connections of booking-search.

record: Wrong prices in search results. After the night import, the search showed yesterday's prices; the booking page showed the new ones. Work notes: the price import finished at 03:10, but the search cache kept the old entries for 24 hours. Resolution: cleared the cache and made the import job clear it.
explanation: The search cache kept serving old prices after the night import.

record: Every connection to Hamburg shown twice. Since the timetable import of the partner rail company, search results listed each connection to Hamburg two times. Work notes: the partner's file contained every Hamburg trip twice; our import accepted the duplicates. Resolution: removed the duplicates, added a duplicate check to the import.
explanation: The partner's timetable file contained duplicate trips that the import accepted.

record: No results for 30 cities. After booking-search release 4.0.0, searches for 30 smaller cities returned no results. Work notes: the new ranking in 4.0.0 drops stations with fewer than 10 departures a day. Resolution: rolled back to 3.9.2; fixed in 4.0.1.
explanation: Release 4.0.0 introduced a ranking rule that dropped small stations.

record: Seat map not loading for a third of the customers. After checkout-web release 1.7.0 the seat map stayed empty. Work notes: the release itself was fine on the test system; the CDN still delivered the JavaScript bundle of 1.6.x to many browsers, which does not match the new API. Resolution: purged the CDN cache.
explanation: The CDN cache kept serving the old JavaScript bundle after the release.

record: Security warning on all checkout pages. Browsers showed a certificate warning from 00:00; most customers left. Work notes: the TLS certificate of the checkout domain expired at midnight; the renewal job had been switched off months ago. Resolution: renewed the certificate, switched the job on, added an expiry alert.
explanation: The TLS certificate of the checkout domain expired because its renewal job was off.

record: Voucher codes rejected. Customers could not redeem the autumn campaign vouchers. Work notes: the campaign end date in the configuration was 2026-10-31 instead of 2026-11-30; no release that week. Resolution: corrected the campaign configuration.
explanation: The campaign end date in the configuration was wrong.

record: Checkout pages blank. For 40 minutes the checkout pages stayed white in most browsers. Work notes: the cookie-consent script, loaded from the vendor's server, did not answer and blocked the page rendering. Our systems were healthy. Resolution: none on our side - the vendor fixed their server.
explanation: The external cookie-consent script did not load and blocked the page; nothing on our side had to be fixed.

record: Disk full on node-7. node-7 ran out of disk space and two pods were evicted. Work notes: log rotation was switched off on node-7 during a debugging session three weeks ago and never switched on again. Traffic was normal. Resolution: switched log rotation on, removed old log files.
explanation: Log rotation was left switched off on node-7, so the logs filled the disk.

record: Ledger queries take seconds. Reports and refunds were delayed because queries on the ledger took several seconds. Work notes: payment-api release 2.2.0 shipped a schema migration that rebuilt the ledger table without its index on booking_id. Resolution: added the index; migration fixed for future releases.
explanation: The schema migration shipped with release 2.2.0 dropped an index on the ledger table.

record: Booking confirmations delayed. Confirmation e-mails arrived up to two hours late. Work notes: marketing sent a mass mailing of 2 million e-mails through the same mail queue; the backlog grew for hours. No change. Resolution: paused the mass mailing, scaled the mail workers.
explanation: A mass mailing filled the shared mail queue, and confirmations waited behind it.

record: Login impossible for business customers. Business customers sign in through their company's external identity provider, which did not answer for 50 minutes. Private customers could log in. Resolution: none on our side - the identity provider recovered.
explanation: The external identity provider of business customers was down; nothing on our side had to be fixed.
